title: A2ASecBench: A Protocol-Aware Security Benchmark for Agent-to-Agent Multi-Agent Systems
pdf_path: papers/A2ASecBench_A Protocol-Aware Security Benchmark for Agent-to-Agent Multi-Agent Systems.pdf
threat_model_summary: Protocol-aware attacker manipulates A2A AgentCards, capabilities and task flows; benchmark measures spoofing, capability cloaking, task hijacking, resource abuse and message attacks. Not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Protocol-aware A2A security benchmark
AgentCard spoofing and capability cloaking attack families
Evaluation across domains and agent frameworks
Shows guardrails only partially mitigate and signature/attestation are suggested, not implemented
limitations: LLM-level benchmark, not protocol-level cryptographic verification
Attacks are lookalike/field perturbations, not signature forgery
theoretical_crypto_links: None; AgentCard signature/attestation is only a prompt-level suggestion (p.9, pp.15-16)
Signed AgentCards and capability attestation are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No JWS, mTLS, credential or registry implementation
Suggested publisher signature/key continuity, TLS, revocation, capability attestation are unimplemented

title: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
pdf_path: papers/OpenAgentSafety_A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety.pdf
threat_model_summary: Evaluates agent behavior on 356 safety tasks with real tools and multi-turn/multi-user interaction; unsafe states are judged by rules and an LLM judge. Not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: OpenAgentSafety framework on OpenHands/Docker with real tools
356 tasks across 8 risk categories
Evaluates 7 models on safety-vulnerable trajectories and full task set
Human study shows LLM-judge unsafe rates are conservative and failure rates overstated
limitations: LLM judge unreliable and rule evaluator task-specific
Docker is OS isolation, not a security architecture
Task coverage and harm categories limited
Conditional rates not deployment risk rates
theoretical_crypto_links: None; no security definition or proof
Policy-compliance game formalization is our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Capability tokens/credential broker/signed audit logs are plausible harness extensions (our inference)

title: Breaking Agent Backbones: Evaluating the Security of Backbone LLMs in AI Agents
pdf_path: papers/Breaking Agent Backbones_Evaluating the Security of Backbone LLMs in AI Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Threat snapshot isolates a single LLM call from an agent execution and tests 30 scenarios with 210 selected attacks from 194,331 crowdsourced attempts across 34 LLMs. Behavioral vulnerability, not cryptographic compromise.
core_contributions: Threat snapshot framework for comparing backbone LLMs
30 snapshots across 10 scenarios and three difficulty levels
210 attacks selected from 194,331 crowdsourced attacks
34-LLM evaluation with bootstrap confidence intervals
limitations: Crowdsourced attacks may not represent adaptive adversaries
System-level closed models include vendor guardrails
theoretical_crypto_links: Context provenance/authentication is our inference, not proof of instruction legitimacy
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Signed/MACed context segments could be a harness variable (our inference)

title: TAMAS: Benchmarking Adversarial Risks in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
pdf_path: papers/TAMAS_Benchmarking Adversarial Risks in Multi-Agent LLM Systems.pdf
threat_model_summary: 300 adversarial instances across 5 domains and 6 attack types against AutoGen/CrewAI configurations; attackers use prompt-level impersonation, direct/indirect injection and collusion. Behavioral, not cryptographic.
core_contributions: TAMAS multi-agent adversarial risk benchmark
5 domains, 300 instances, 6 attack types, 100 harmless tasks
Evaluation of 10 backbone LLMs and 5 configurations
Safety-utility metric and defense evaluation
limitations: 'Byzantine' and 'collusion' are behavioral labels, not BFT/cryptographic models
Relative min-max scoring; no per-domain breakdown
theoretical_crypto_links: None; impersonation is an unauthenticated authority claim but the threat model also rewrites user queries
Signed agent identity/role credentials are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Signed agent cards and authenticated inter-agent messages are plausible harness extensions

title: ACIArena: Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection
pdf_path: papers/ACIArena_Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection.pdf
threat_model_summary: Attacker injects through external input, malicious agent profiles or inter-agent messages to achieve hijacking, task disruption or data exfiltration in multi-agent systems; benchmark measures propagation. Behavioral, not cryptographic.
core_contributions: ACI taxonomy across three attack surfaces and three goals
28 attack types and 1,356 cases generated with mutation plus LLM judge
Evaluation of six MAS frameworks and three LLMs with BU/ASR/UA/PVI
ACI-SENTINEL semantic minimization defense
limitations: Behavioral benchmark; no protocol-level cryptographic instrumentation
LLM-judge and mutation pipeline may bias attacks
theoretical_crypto_links: None; cascading injection is not a cryptographic propagation/authentication chain
Authenticated inter-agent messages are our inference and do not stop semantic injection
applied_crypto_links: Signed/authenticated agent messages are a peripheral control only
